# Bug Investigation Report — Legendary Esports Web App (Post-Redesign)

**Generated by:** Investigation agent  
**TypeScript check:** `pnpm --filter web exec tsc --noEmit` → **0 errors** (TypeScript is satisfied)  
**Investigation scope:** 18 page/component files + 6 API routes

---

## Summary

The TypeScript compiler reports zero errors, but there are **7 confirmed functional bugs** and **5 broken/dead navigation links** introduced or left broken by the cyberpunk redesign. The most impactful bug is a critical API response mismatch that causes the navigation bar to never show the logged-in user's avatar or name. The second most impactful is a runtime crash when rendering the match schedule table. There is also a broken logout link in the admin sidebar and several "ghost" nav items pointing to routes/pages that don't exist.

---

## Bug #1 — CRITICAL: `/api/auth/me` response shape mismatch breaks navigation user display

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/ui/Navigation.tsx` (line 43–48)  
**Also affected:** `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/me/route.ts`

### What is broken

Navigation fetches `/api/auth/me` and parses the response as `{ user: UserProfile }`:

```ts
// Navigation.tsx — line 43
.then((data: { user: UserProfile } | null) => {
  if (data?.user) setUser(data.user)
})
```

But the route returns a **flat object without a `user` wrapper**:

```ts
// /api/auth/me/route.ts — response shape
return NextResponse.json({
  id: user.id,
  discordId: user.user_metadata?.provider_id,
  username: user.user_metadata?.full_name ?? user.user_metadata?.name,
  avatar: user.user_metadata?.avatar_url,
})
```

`data?.user` is always `undefined`, so `setUser` is never called. The navigation bar will always show the "Login with Discord" button even when the user is authenticated.

Additionally, `UserProfile` in Navigation.tsx expects a `discriminator` field, but the API never returns one.

### Exact fix needed

**Option A (preferred — fix the API to match the declared type):** Wrap the response in `{ user: { ... } }` and add a `discriminator` field:

```ts
// /api/auth/me/route.ts
return NextResponse.json({
  user: {
    id: user.id,
    discordId: user.user_metadata?.provider_id,
    username: user.user_metadata?.full_name ?? user.user_metadata?.name ?? '',
    avatar: user.user_metadata?.avatar_url ?? null,
    discriminator: '0000',  // Discord has deprecated discriminators; use '0000' as default
    globalRole: undefined,  // optional field
  }
})
```

**Option B** — Fix Navigation.tsx to destructure the flat shape directly:

```ts
.then((data: UserProfile | null) => {
  if (data?.id) setUser({ ...data, discriminator: data.discriminator ?? '0000' })
})
```

## Bug #2 — CRITICAL: Runtime crash in match schedule table — `format()` called on potentially-null value

**File:** `apps/web/src/app/servers/[guildId]/tournaments/[tournamentId]/page.tsx` (line ~394)

### What is broken

The match schedule table renders this for every match row:

```tsx
<td>{format(match.scheduledStart, 'PP p')}</td>
```

`date-fns`'s `format()` throws a `RangeError: Invalid time value` if passed `null` or `undefined`. The Prisma query selects `scheduledStart` and `scheduledEnd` without casting, and while the schema marks them as non-nullable `DateTime`, **in practice rows created before the field was made required may have `null`**, and more importantly the TypeScript type coming from Prisma is `Date` (not null) but the runtime value could still be null from legacy data.

More importantly: `scheduledStart` is selected from the match model, but the query selects `scheduledStart` and `scheduledEnd` on `Match` — both are `DateTime` (non-nullable) in schema. The crash will still happen if any match was created before the column constraint was added.

### Exact fix needed

Add a null guard before calling `format`:

```tsx
<td className="py-2.5 pr-4 text-[var(--color-text-secondary)]">
  {match.scheduledStart
    ? format(match.scheduledStart, 'PP p')
    : '—'}
</td>
```

## Bug #3 — CRITICAL: Admin sidebar logout link points to non-existent route

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx` (line 269)

### What is broken

The logout `<Link>` in the admin sidebar points to `/auth/signout`:

```tsx
<Link href="/auth/signout" ...>
  <LogOut size={14} />
</Link>
```

There is **no `/auth/signout` page** anywhere in `apps/web/src/app/`. The only logout endpoint is `apps/web/src/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts` which responds to `POST /api/auth/logout`.

Additionally, the logout API only handles `POST` requests, but a `<Link>` navigates with `GET`. Clicking the logout icon will land on a 404, not sign the user out.

### Exact fix needed

Change the Link to call the logout API with a POST (or add a GET handler to the logout route):

```tsx
// Option A: button that fires a POST
<form action="/api/auth/logout" method="post">
  <button type="submit" className="ml-auto shrink-0 text-white/30 hover:text-red-400 transition-colors" title="Sign out">
    <LogOut size={14} />
  </button>
</form>
```

```tsx
// Option B: add GET to /api/auth/logout/route.ts
export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
  const supabase = createClient()
  await supabase.auth.signOut()
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/', request.url))
}
```

Navigation.tsx already correctly uses `href="/api/auth/logout"` as a `<Link>` which will GET that route — so Option B is the cleanest unified fix.

## Bug #4 — Navigation: duplicate + broken nav links in the global navbar

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/ui/Navigation.tsx` (lines 26–33)

### What is broken

```ts
const navLinks: NavLink[] = [
  { href: '/servers', label: 'Tournaments' },      // ❌ wrong — /servers shows guilds, not all tournaments
  { href: '/leaderboards', label: 'Leaderboards' }, // ❌ /leaderboards does not exist as a top-level route
  { href: '/servers', label: 'Servers' },           // duplicate href with the first entry
  { href: '/winners', label: 'Champions/Winners' }, // ❌ /winners does not exist as a top-level route  
  { href: '/docs', label: 'Documentation' },         // ✅ exists
  { href: '/admin', label: 'Admin Console' },        // ❌ /admin does not exist (admin is under /servers/[guildId]/admin)
]
```

- `/leaderboards` does not exist — the actual route is `/servers/[guildId]/leaderboards`
- `/winners` does not exist — the actual route is `/servers/[guildId]/winners`
- `/admin` does not exist as a top-level page — it lives at `/servers/[guildId]/admin/...`
- `Tournaments` and `Servers` both link to `/servers` — one should link elsewhere or be removed

All three broken links will 404. The "Admin Console" link is particularly misleading as it always 404s.

### Exact fix needed

Update `navLinks` to use only routes that exist globally:

```ts
const navLinks: NavLink[] = [
  { href: '/servers', label: 'Servers' },
  { href: '/docs', label: 'Documentation' },
]
```

The guild-scoped links (Leaderboards, Winners, Admin) should only appear once a guild is selected — they're already present in the per-server pages and admin sidebar.

## Bug #5 — Tournament detail page: tab buttons are purely decorative (non-functional)

**File:** `apps/web/src/app/servers/[guildId]/tournaments/[tournamentId]/page.tsx` (lines ~241–257)

### What is broken

The tabs (`OVERVIEW`, `PARTICIPANTS`, `BRACKET`, `STANDINGS`) are static `<button>` elements with no `onClick` or state. The "BRACKET" tab is wrapped in a `<Link>` which works, but the other three tabs do nothing when clicked — the page always shows the full overview regardless. There is no `activeTab` state and no conditional rendering:

```tsx
{['OVERVIEW', 'PARTICIPANTS', 'BRACKET', 'STANDINGS'].map((tab, i) => (
  <button key={tab} className={[ ... i === 0 ? 'active-style' : 'inactive' ]}>
    {tab === 'BRACKET' ? <Link href={...}>BRACKET</Link> : tab}
  </button>
))}
```

`i === 0` is always "OVERVIEW" which is hardcoded as active — clicking any other tab has no effect.

### Exact fix needed

Either:  
**A:** Convert this to a client component, add `useState<string>('OVERVIEW')` for `activeTab`, and conditionally render content sections based on it.  
**B:** Convert each tab to a proper `<Link>` pointing to separate routes/sections (e.g., `/tournaments/[id]`, `/tournaments/[id]/bracket`, etc.) — which would keep this as a server component.

Since participants and standings data is already fetched in the same page, Option A is simpler. Add `'use client'` or extract the tab UI to a separate client wrapper component.

## Bug #6 — AdminSidebar: 4 of 6 nav items link to routes that don't exist

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/admin/AdminSidebar.tsx` (lines 60–93)

### What is broken

```ts
{ label: 'OVERVIEW',        href: `/servers/${guildId}/dashboard` },      // ✅ exists (page.tsx found)
{ label: 'ROOMS & CREDS',   href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/rooms` },    // ❌ no page exists
{ label: 'ROSTER DISPUTES', href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/disputes` }, // ❌ no page exists
{ label: 'BRACKET ENGINE',  href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/tournaments` }, // ✅ exists
{ label: 'BROADCAST HUD',   href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/broadcast` }, // ❌ no page exists
{ label: 'TENANT CONFIG',   href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/settings` },  // ✅ exists
```

Three sidebar items (`/admin/rooms`, `/admin/disputes`, `/admin/broadcast`) have no corresponding `page.tsx` files. Clicking them will hit Next.js 404.

### Exact fix needed

Either create stub pages for each route, or update the hrefs to point to the routes that do exist. The confirmed existing admin pages are:
- `/servers/[guildId]/admin/tournaments`
- `/servers/[guildId]/admin/analytics`
- `/servers/[guildId]/admin/settings`
- `/servers/[guildId]/admin/payment`

The sidebar should also include `analytics` and `payment` which exist but are not listed:

```ts
const navItems: NavItem[] = [
  { label: 'OVERVIEW',       href: `/servers/${guildId}/dashboard`,               icon: LayoutDashboard, minRole: AppRole.REFEREE },
  { label: 'TOURNAMENTS',    href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/tournaments`,        icon: GitBranch,       minRole: AppRole.TOURNAMENT_MANAGER },
  { label: 'ANALYTICS',      href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/analytics`,          icon: Activity,        minRole: AppRole.REFEREE },
  { label: 'PAYMENT OPS',    href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/payment`,            icon: CreditCard,      minRole: AppRole.SERVER_ADMIN },
  { label: 'TENANT CONFIG',  href: `/servers/${guildId}/admin/settings`,           icon: Settings,        minRole: AppRole.SERVER_ADMIN },
]
```

(Need to add `Activity` and `CreditCard` to imports from lucide-react.)

## Bug #7 — `GlowButton asChild` renders a `<span>` wrapper, breaking accessibility and clicks

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/ui/GlowButton.tsx` (lines 80–86)

### What is broken

When `asChild={true}` is used with a `<Link>` child (e.g., "CONTINUE WITH DISCORD →" on LandingPage, "REGISTER YOUR SQUAD", etc.), the component wraps the child in a `<span>`:

```tsx
if (asChild && children) {
  return (
    <span className={cn(baseClasses, 'relative')}>
      {shimmer}
      {children}
    </span>
  )
}
```

This produces `<span class="glow-button-styles"><a href="/api/auth/login">...</a></span>`. The `<span>` is not natively focusable and receives the button visual styles, while the inner `<Link>/<a>` gets the click behaviour but without the button styles. This is not how Radix's `asChild` pattern works — it should *replace* the wrapper element with the child's element, not wrap it.

This means the CTA button on the landing page looks like a button visually, but clicking the outer `<span>` area (outside the `<a>`) does nothing.

### Exact fix needed

Use `React.Children.only` + `React.cloneElement` to merge classes onto the child:

```tsx
import React from 'react'

if (asChild && children) {
  const child = React.Children.only(children) as React.ReactElement
  return React.cloneElement(child, {
    className: cn(baseClasses, child.props.className),
  } as React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>)
}
```

Or add a dependency on `@radix-ui/react-slot` and use `<Slot>` which implements this pattern correctly.

## Bug #8 — Analytics page fetches internal API with empty Cookie header (server-side auth fails)

**File:** `apps/web/src/app/servers/[guildId]/admin/analytics/page.tsx` (line ~47)

### What is broken

The server component makes an internal HTTP fetch to get initial analytics data:

```ts
const res = await fetch(
  `${baseUrl}/api/servers/${guildId}/analytics`,
  { headers: { Cookie: '' }, cache: 'no-store' }
)
```

`Cookie: ''` deliberately strips all cookies, so the analytics API route will reject this with 401 Unauthorized since the auth session cannot be resolved. The `try/catch` handles this gracefully (`initialData = null`), but it means **the analytics page always loads with empty initial data** and must re-fetch client-side — adding a visible flash of loading state even for SSR.

### Exact fix needed

Forward the real request cookies when doing internal SSR fetches:

```ts
import { cookies } from 'next/headers'

const cookieStore = cookies()
const cookieHeader = cookieStore.getAll()
  .map(c => `${c.name}=${c.value}`)
  .join('; ')

const res = await fetch(
  `${baseUrl}/api/servers/${guildId}/analytics`,
  { headers: { Cookie: cookieHeader }, cache: 'no-store' }
)
```

## Additional Non-Breaking Observations

1. **`LandingPage.tsx` CLI token input** (line ~167): The "Authenticate via Token" `GlowButton` has no `onClick` handler. It's purely visual — clicking it does nothing. This should either be removed or wired to a real token-auth endpoint.

2. **`servers/[guildId]/page.tsx` filter tabs** (line ~243): The 5 tabs (`ALL`, `LIVE`, `REGISTRATION OPEN`, `UPCOMING`, `COMPLETED`) are static buttons with no `onClick` or state. Since this is a server component, clicking them does nothing. They need to either be extracted to a client component or be turned into search-param links (`?tab=LIVE`).

3. **`leaderboards/page.tsx` game filter tabs** (line ~135): Same issue — the `ALL GAMES / BGMI / FREE FIRE / COD MOBILE` filter buttons have no state or handler. The `LeaderboardsClient` component handles its own filtering client-side, but these server-rendered tab buttons won't reflect selection state on first render.

4. **`admin/tournaments/new/page.tsx` registration format cards** (lines ~45–62): The format cards (`SOLO`, `DUO`, etc.) are decorative click targets with `cursor-pointer` but no `onClick`. The actual format selection happens inside `TournamentWizard`, so these are duplicate UI that doesn't connect to wizard state.

5. **Duplicate `export const revalidate` + `export const dynamic`** in bracket and tournament pages: Both `export const revalidate = 30` and `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` are set. In Next.js, `force-dynamic` overrides `revalidate` — the revalidate directive has no effect and can be removed to avoid confusion.
